title: Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Digital Television) Bill 2006
portfolio: Communications, Information Technology and the Arts

speeches.speaker: Sandy Macdonald
speeches.brief: Senator Coonan moved to introduce four bills: amending broadcasting law, the Broadcasting Services Act 1992, the Crimes Act 1914, and prudential regulation for trans-Tasman cooperation. The bills were agreed to and read a first time without formalities.

speeches.speaker: Sandy Macdonald
speeches.brief: The speaker introduced four bills: digital television reforms removing genre restrictions and phasing multichannelling for commercial broadcasters, with anti-siphoning protections maintained; media ownership reforms removing foreign ownership restrictions and relaxing cross-media rules while requiring minimum diversity of five media groups in capitals and four elsewhere, plus local content conditions; bail and sentencing amendments preventing customary law or cultural practice from mitigating criminal sentences or bail decisions; and trans-Tasman banking supervision amendments requiring APRA to support the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and consider financial system stability in New Zealand.

speeches.speaker: Michael Ronaldson
speeches.brief: The government argued the media ownership bills would modernise outdated laws and benefit consumers through greater competition and new digital services, while Labor and the Democrats opposed the changes, warning they would reduce media diversity and concentrate ownership in the hands of a few large companies. The government agreed to a "two out of three" rule preventing a single owner from controlling all three of commercial TV, radio and a newspaper in any licence area, and to require regional radio stations to broadcast at least 4.5 hours of local content and 12.5 minutes of local news daily.

Senator Sandy Macdonald moved that four media and communications bills be read a second time, including the Communications Legislation Amendment (Enforcement Powers) Bill 2006, Television Licence Fees Amendment Bill 2006, Broadcasting Services Amendment (Media Ownership) Bill 2006, and Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Digital Television) Bill 2006.

speeches.speaker: Lyn Allison
speeches.brief: The government argued that media ownership reforms, including a two-out-of-three rule and local content mandates, are necessary to modernise outdated laws for the digital age and benefit consumers. Opponents countered that the changes would reduce media diversity, concentrate power, and harm regional communities.

speeches.speaker: Helen Coonan
speeches.brief: The government argued that the media ownership and digital television bills would reform outdated media laws, allowing cross-media mergers with safeguards such as a minimum of five media groups in mainland state capitals and four in other areas, a two-out-of-three rule, and local content requirements, while enabling new digital services including an HD multichannel from 2007 and an SD multichannel from 2009, and a "use it or lose it" system for antisiphoning sports from 2007.

speeches.speaker: Ian Macdonald
speeches.brief: The senator argued that the legislation's local content requirements could force unprofitable regional radio stations, such as those in Mareeba and Roma, to shut down, and that overregulation risked reducing media diversity in country areas. He supported the local content amendments as a necessary protection but called for more flexibility, noting that the minister had adopted some committee recommendations.
